why.compile.job_mb: the most memory one compile may take: the recompiled C is cut into units that fit it (recomp/units.py), and the jobs that run at once share what the device has free
why.compile.base_mb: a compile's memory before its C: the compiler with the runtime's headers, and Zig's driver
why.compile.mb_per_mib_of_c: what each MiB of a unit's C adds to its compile's peak (measured over units of 4 KB to 2 MB)
why.compile.reserve_mb: memory left to the system and the app while compiling: the jobs never count on it
why.compile.poll_s: how often the free memory is read again while compiling (the jobs come down when it does)
why.translation.peak_mb: the translation's peak memory (one process: the analysis of the whole code, then its C), checked before it starts
why.space.dump_mb: the executable and its header extracted from the update
why.space.objects_mb: the compiled objects (the cache shares their files when it can)
why.space.zig_copies_mb: Zig's own copy of each object while compiling
why.space.library_mb: the library, made beside the objects, then copied to the game's folder
why.space.cache_floor_mb: the least the objects' cache keeps (one build's objects), so a mod update compiles only what changed
why.cache.keep_free_mb: the cache grows only while this much of the disk stays free; past it the oldest objects go
why.cache.max_mb: the most the cache keeps whatever the free space
